basics.name: Konrad Odell
basics.label: Staff Engineer, Architecture · Applied AI & Healthcare Data
basics.summary: I've been shipping software for twenty years and setting technical direction since 2018. I'm on the architecture team at Moxe Health, a HIPAA-regulated clinical data exchange (joined 2022, architecture team since 2024), working on the Databricks lakehouse, FHIR pipelines, and evaluating LLM and agent approaches against real clinical and billing workloads. On my own time I built and run ElectricityFinder, which runs an LLM extraction pipeline in production in a regulated market, and the tooling I build with: MCP servers, agent skills, and evaluation harnesses. I build with coding agents in a worker and verifier loop: a separate agent with fresh context has to prove the work runs before I accept it.

Driving canary deploys, smoke tests, and auto-rollback as first-class patterns in the new platform architecture (in progress)

projects.name: Agentic Engineering Estate
projects.summary: A working multi-agent development system used daily to build and verify the projects on this page — the practice behind treating AI coding agents as production build tools.
highlights: Reusable building blocks: a library of 68 agent skills (usage-instrumented and pruned by actual fire-count), 45 deterministic hooks, MCP servers and tool adapters in daily production use, and sub-agent/workflow orchestration patterns

Custom eval harnesses rather than vibes: an own-commit SWE-bench-style benchmark for scoring local and frontier models on real repository work, plus adversarial-eval and domain-specific benches. Caught a model reading the answer from git history, closed the leak, and re-audited all 122 prior runs

Deterministic orchestration with worker/verifier separation: unattended overnight agent runs fixed 8 ElectricityFinder bugs, each re-verified from a clean checkout by a separate agent; deploys stayed human-approved
Belief-state engine pairing LLM extraction with deterministic code judges, over a hybrid lexical + semantic search layer
Multi-provider routing in practice (Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google, and local open-weight models behind one gateway), plus local serving and LoRA fine-tuning on consumer hardware
